bakedProductMatrices.name: Fermented Soda Cracker (High Starch, Rapid Checking Susceptibility, 1.2% Salt, pH 7.2)
bakedProductMatrices.description: Multi-layered laminated cracker with high moisture gradient between internal lamellae and crispy edges. Extreme vulnerability to post-bake checking if moisture difference exceeds 2.5% at packaging.

bakedProductMatrices.name: Hard Sweet Biscuit (Marie / Petit Beurre - Wheat Flour, 19% Sugar, 11% Fat)
bakedProductMatrices.description: Dense rotary-molded dough with compact crumb structure. Conventional oven drying darkens the surface excessively; RF selective heating evaporates center moisture with zero surface caramelization.

bakedProductMatrices.name: Wholemeal Digestive Cookie (Coarse Bran, High Density, 16% Fat, 15% Sugar)
bakedProductMatrices.description: Thick cross-section wholemeal biscuit with high hygroscopic moisture capacity. High center moisture requires deep 27.12 MHz penetration to prevent core mold proliferation and structural crumb collapse.

bakedProductMatrices.name: Gluten-Free Rice & Corn Starch Wafer (Fragile Porous Crumb, Low Fat, 0.5% Salt)
bakedProductMatrices.description: Thin, highly brittle wafer sheets with minimal tensile strength. Without RF moisture equilibration, uneven moisture causes severe warping, breakage during cream application, and packaging line jams.

dielectricLossMechanisms.physicsPrinciple: Water molecules (permanent electric dipoles) continuously oscillate in phase with the alternating RF electric field, generating volumetric frictional heat predominantly in moisture-rich pockets.
dielectricLossMechanisms.energyEfficiencyPct: 88% to 94% selective coupling to free liquid water

dielectricLossMechanisms.physicsPrinciple: Dissolved ionic salts (Na+, Cl-, K+) migrate electrophoretically between RF electrode poles with each half-cycle. In high-salt localized pockets, ionic conduction adds to dielectric loss, requiring runaway monitoring.
dielectricLossMechanisms.energyEfficiencyPct: Increases sharply with temperature if salt > 1.5%

dielectricLossMechanisms.physicsPrinciple: Dry baked starch, gluten protein, and crystallized shortening have near-zero dielectric loss factor (ε'' < 0.4), rendering them essentially transparent to the RF field and immune to overheating.
dielectricLossMechanisms.energyEfficiencyPct: < 5% RF power absorption in dry areas

regulatoryStandards.title: Establishment of Mitigation Measures and Benchmark Levels for the Reduction of Acrylamide in Food
regulatoryStandards.rfBenefit: RF post-bake drying decouples final moisture removal from oven temperature, cutting acrylamide formation by 50% to 75% compared to extended thermal baking.

regulatoryStandards.title: Occupational Non-Ionizing Electromagnetic Radiation Exposure Limits (RF & Microwave)
regulatoryStandards.benchmarkLevel: Maximum power density 10 mW/cm² (equivalent electric field strength ~61.4 V/m) at 27.12 MHz
regulatoryStandards.rfBenefit: Solid aluminum Faraday cage enclosure with entrance/exit RF suppression chokes ensures ambient operator radiation remains < 0.5 mW/cm² (>20x safety factor).

regulatoryStandards.code: NFPA 86 Standard for Ovens and Furnaces

regulatoryStandards.benchmarkLevel: Automatic high-speed RF generator shutdown (<5 ms) upon optical flash, arc detection, or conveyor stall
